sentences.text: Shri D.P.Singh, learned counsel for the petitioner .

Shri Vineet, Pl appearing on behalf of Advocate Gener
 Shri Vibhor Kumar Sahu, learned counsel for the respo
 Reserved on : 28.11.2025
Pronounced on : 10/12/2025

This petition having been heard and reserved for orders, Hon'
 Milind Ramesh Phadke, Judge pronounced the following:
 Order

The petitioner has filed the present petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure seeking quashing of the FIR bearing Crime No. 0690/2023 (Annexure A/1) registered by respondent No. 1, on the basis of the application submitted by respondent No. 2 (complainant)
alleging offences under Sections 376, 376(2)(n), and 506 of the IPC and for quashing of all consequential proceedings arising from the said FIR.
2. As per the prosecution story, the complainant alleges that about four years ago, in 2019, she came into contact with the petitioner through phone chats.

They became acquainted with each other, and the petitioner allegedly NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:31268 2 MCRC-57683-2023 assured her that he would marry her since they both belong to the same caste.

On the basis of this assurance, the petitioner allegedly began visiting the complainant at her rented room in Bhargav Vishnu Kumar Bairwa vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 28 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140173871/
1 Colony, Guna, and established physical relations with her on several occasions.

entities.text: Bhargav Vishnu Kumar Bairwa vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 28 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The complainant further alleges that on 02.01.2022, when she asked the petitioner to marry her, he refused and allegedly told her that he has affairs with many girls and cannot marry all of them.
She also claims that he threatened to defame her and kill her if she made any complaint.

Based on these allegations,
the FIR under Sections 376, 376(2)(n), and 506 IPC was registered against the petitioner.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the FIR is malicious, arbitrary, and an abuse of the process of law.
The relationship between the petitioner and the complainant was completely consensual.
The allegations are an afterthought and have been made only to harass the petitioner.
It is submitted that the complainant voluntarily entered into a relationship with the petitioner out of her own free will and independent decision.
There was no force, coercion, or deception at any stage.
The complainant was fully aware of the nature of the relationship.
The WhatsApp conversations exchanged between the parties clearly show that their relationship was consensual and based on mutual affection.
The chats do not reveal any false promise of marriage, but only normal interaction between two consenting adults.
It is submitted that the case is not one of a false promise of marriage, but at most a case where the relationship broke down due to differences and unavoidable circumstances.
Mere failure to marry does not amount to rape under Section 376 IPC.

To bolster his submission NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:31268 3 MCRC-57683-2023 learned counsel for the petitioner placed reliance on the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ansaar Mohammad vs. State of Rajasthan, reported in 2022 Live Law SC 599, wherein it was held that when a relationship is consensual and long-standing, failure of the relationship cannot be a ground for filing an FIR under Section 376 IPC.

entities.text: Ansaar Mohammad vs. State of Rajasthan, reported in 2022 Live Law SC 599
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is argued that this case is a typical example of breach of promise, not a false promise.
The complainant continued the relationship willingly for years and stayed with the petitioner on multiple occasions.
There is no material to show that the petitioner ever intended to deceive her from the beginning.
It is submitted that the complainant lodged the FIR only after the relationship deteriorated, which shows that the FIR is motivated and based on personal vengeance.

It is further submitted that after registration of the FIR, the complainant's advocate contacted the petitioner and tried to settle the matter by asking him to compensate the complainant financially in exchange for her turning hostile.
WhatsApp chats between the petitioner and the complainant's advocate (Annexure A/4) clearly indicate an attempt to misuse criminal law to extort money.
This shows that the FIR is not genuine and is filed only for ulterior motives.

Learned counsel submits that the case squarely falls under the principles laid down in State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal , reported in AIR 1992 SC 604, where the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that FIRs can be quashed where allegations do not disclose any offence, material collected does not support the allegations, criminal law is being misused for personal motives, and the FIR is manifestly attended with mala fide intentions.

entities.text: State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal , reported in AIR 1992 SC 604
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, it was submitted that the proceedings instituted against the present petitioners NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:31268 4 MCRC-57683-2023 deserve to be quashed in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the matter of Bhajan Lal (supra).

4. Per contra, Counsel for the respondent/State as well as Counsel for the respondent No.2 had opposed the submissions so made by counsel for the petitioner and it was submitted that there are specific allegations against the present petitioner, therefore, he is not entitled for any relief and inherent powers under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. cannot be exercised.

It was further submitted that the Vishnu Kumar Bairwa vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 28 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140173871/
2 First Information Report speaks volumes about the conduct of the present petitioner and as per the First Information Report, prima facie a case is made out against petitioner under the aforesaid sections and, therefore, no interference is warranted.
5. Heard counsel for the parties and perused the record.
6.

entities.text: Vishnu Kumar Bairwa vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 28 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: From perusal of the record, it is clear that the allegations made by the complainant clearly disclose the commission of cognizable offences under Sections 376, 376(2)(n), and 506 of the IPC.
The complainant has specifically stated that the petitioner established physical relations with her repeatedly on the assurance of marriage and later refused to marry her and threatened her.
These allegations, at this stage, cannot be brushed aside as false or motivated, nor can it be concluded that the relationship was purely consensual, as claimed by the petitioner.
The contradictions or defence of consensual relations are matters that can be examined only during trial after appreciation of evidence.

The reliance placed by the petitioner on the WhatsApp chats and the judgments cited,
including Ansaar Mohammad vs. State of Rajasthan, is misplaced because the question whether the promise of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:31268 5 MCRC-57683-2023 marriage was false from the very inception, whether consent was obtained under misconception, and whether the petitioner intended to deceive the complainant, are all matters of fact which require detailed examination of evidence.

entities.text: Ansaar Mohammad vs. State of Rajasthan
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Likewise, the allegations regarding alleged settlement attempts by the complainant's advocate cannot be considered at this stage without proper proof and cannot be a ground to quash criminal proceedings.
7. Furthermore, the parameters laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Bhajan Lal (supra) do not assist the petitioner.
The FIR discloses a cognizable offence, and the facts of the present case do not fall under any of the categories warranting interference under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
This Court cannot, in the exercise of inherent jurisdiction, conduct a mini-trial or test the defence of the accused at this preliminary stage.

8. After considering the submissions made on behalf of the petitioner and upon perusal of the case diary, FIR, statements, and other material placed on record, this Court is of the view that no ground is made out for exercising inherent powers under Section 482 Cr.P.C. to quash the FIR or the consequential proceedings.
9. In view of the above discussion, this Court finds no merit in the present petition.
The petition under Section 528 of BNSS/section 482 Cr.P.C. is accordingly dismissed.
(MILIND RAMESH PHADKE) JUDGE (aspr)
